_comment: SYNTHETIC — hand-built from the documented response shapes in Yahoo's official
Fantasy Sports API guide and from published wrapper-library samples (yfpy,
yahoo_fantasy_api). NOT a live capture. Yahoo API access is gated behind an
approval application and NO live call has ever been made from this repo.
Replace with a real redacted capture once API access is approved.
AUTHORED 2026-08-11 (not captured on any date).
MODELS: GET /fantasy/v2/league/461.l.576919/transactions?format=json
(one add/drop transaction extracted from that collection)
REDACTION: all identifiers invented — team keys, team names and transaction
ids are fake. Player names are real NFL players with PLAUSIBLE BUT UNVERIFIED
numeric ids. No token, email, real GUID or real league key appears here.
WHY THIS IS COMMITTED: this is the BARE-DICT half of the transaction_data
shape trap. For an add/drop, Yahoo sends transaction_data as a plain object;
for a trade it sends a LIST OF ONE OBJECT (see
yahoo_transaction_trade_multi.json). Code written against either shape alone
silently drops one hundred percent of the other kind — no exception, no
warning, just a transaction log missing every trade or every waiver move.
parse_transactions() runs both through as_list(), and this fixture is the
half that proves the collapsed-object branch of iter_collection() is live.
SHAPE HAZARDS DELIBERATELY PRESENT:
1. transaction_data is a BARE DICT here. iter_collection() must hit its
'non-numeric key → this is a single collapsed element' branch and yield
the object itself.
2. 'transaction' is a heterogeneous ARRAY: [ {metadata}, {players: {...}} ].
3. Inside each player, the metadata is a LIST NESTED INSIDE THE RESOURCE
ARRAY — 'player': [ [ {k:v}, {k:v}, ... ], { transaction_data } ] — with
ONE SINGLE-KEY DICT PER FIELD. flatten_resource() has to descend one
extra level for that. This is the shape that breaks naive [0]/[1]
indexing, and it is Yahoo's normal player serialization, not an edge
case.
4. The two legs have OPPOSITE movement types on the SAME transaction: leg 0
type 'add' (source_type 'freeagents', so NO source_team_key exists), leg
1 type 'drop' (source_type 'team' WITH a source_team_key, destination
'waivers' with no destination_team_key). Absent is not empty: a leg with
source_team_key = '' would be a different claim about the world, and
filling the absence with '' destroys the ability to tell a waiver claim
from a free-agent pickup.
5. NO faab_bid key on this transaction. This is a first-come free-agent
add, so 'not exposed' — NULL — not a zero bid. The zero-vs-null contrast
is in yahoo_transaction_faab_waiver.json.
6. Yahoo's own transaction_id is a bare string '142' while transaction_key
is fully qualified; only the key is unique across leagues.
NOT TRUNCATED: this is one complete transaction, deliberately isolated from
the surrounding collection so a failure here is unambiguous.
